title: Lightweight hypothesis router for speculative decode with graceful fallback
creator: Asha Ramesh
description: Implement a compact "lightweight hypothesis router" in the runtime that picks 1-2 speculative decode candidates (fast cheap model, kernel-favorable variant) based on a short prefill probe and a kernel-fingerprint score. The router must produce an acceptance score per candidate and execute a soft-commit path if the optimistic candidate's acceptance >= threshold; otherwise fall back to the conservative decode. Goal: reduce p99 token latency and lower cost by opportunistically using cheaper kernels without impacting output quality beyond an acceptable delta.
background: We've seen workloads with short-turn dialogues where a shallow prefilling probe can predict acceptability of a cheap model candidate (quantized kernel) for the next N tokens. Existing large speculative routing specs are heavy-weight; this ticket targets a minimal, low-risk runtime shim that can be A/Bed and rolled back quickly. Ties into ongoing kernel fingerprint work and KV cache gating experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Router selects candidate within 1ms median decision overhead under load
When enabled for canary subset, 95th token generation latency reduces by >= 8% vs baseline for targeted traffic
Acceptance metric (agreement with golden decoder on greedy next-token) >= 0.82 across sample prompt set for canary traffic
Fallback path triggers for acceptance < threshold with no observable user errors
Telemetry emitted: candidate_id, kernel_fingerprint, acceptance_score, decision_latency, fallback_reason
Config flags exist: enable, threshold, max_candidates=2, probe_length, soft_commit_ttl
design_notes: Keep decision logic in C++ runtime hot path; delegate heavy scoring to a precomputed kernel_fingerprint table
Probe design: 8–12 token prefill probe synthesized from initial request prefix; probe must avoid material state mutation (read-only KV cache)
Acceptance heuristic: linear combination of kernel_affinity_score and short-probe agreement with candidate's greedy outputs
Soft-commit semantics: optimistic candidate writes only to ephemeral commit buffer; commit made durable after N downstream tokens or explicit acceptance signal
Rollback: on either low acceptance score or explicit mismatch metric, route to conservative decoder and drain ephemeral buffer
Config granularity: per-customer, per-model-family, and per-route override
Avoid global autoscale churn by bounding speculative pool size and tracking burst consumption
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement router shim + kernel_fingerprint table + basic probe generation (unit tests)
Phase 2 (integration): wire up candidate invocation path, soft-commit buffer, and fallback plumbing; add telemetry emission
Phase 3 (canary): enable on 1% of production traffic behind feature flag with tight SLO checks
Phase 4 (rollout): expand to 10%/25% with metric gates and runbook for automatic rollback
Phase 5 (post-rollout): iterate tuning thresholds and add small ML scorer if heuristics insufficient
test_plan: Unit tests for decision logic & threshold boundaries
Integration test that forces acceptance and forced fallback paths (deterministic kernels)
Synthetic load test to validate decision overhead under 90% GPU util
A/B experiment comparing canary vs control on latency, cost, and next-token agreement
Regression tests for KV-cache consistency after soft-commit/rollback
Chaos test: induce candidate OOM / kernel failure and assert immediate fallback
rollout_plan: Initial canary: 1% of traffic for 48 hours; require no >10% relative degradation in next-token agreement
Gate checks at 24h and 48h: decision_latency p99, fallback_rate, quality metrics
Progressive ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% with automated rollback if any gate fails
Emergency rollback: feature flag off and invalidate soft-commit buffers across nodes
Post-mortem trigger if rollback caused customer-visible errors
operational_playbook: If router.fallback_rate spikes > 5x baseline: toggle canary off and open PagerDuty if customer-impacting
If decision_latency p99 > 10ms: throttle probe frequency and reduce max_candidates
On kernel mismatch errors: pin problematic kernel variant and mark candidate unhealthy
When increasing rollout, ensure autoscaler has cushion for speculative pool usage
